notes: Independent Bible churches have no binding confession; each congregation writes its own statement of faith. The two documents used are representative, not binding: (1) the Articles of Faith and Doctrine of IFCA International (founded 1930 as the Independent Fundamental Churches of America, per common reference works; the founding date was NOT on the page opened and should be checked before printing), the largest fellowship of independent Bible churches, whose members must subscribe to the articles; and (2) the Doctrinal Statement of Dallas Theological Seminary, the school most associated with the Bible church movement. Neither page opened prints an adoption or revision date, so none is given; do not supply one from memory. The IFCA PDF was reached from https://www.ifca.org/page/doctrinal-statement-clarification ('Our Mission & Doctrine'), which is the stable page to link since the CDN file name may change. All IFCA excerpts were read directly from the PDF text; the DTS excerpts were confirmed against the raw HTML of the page with a text search. Apostrophes in excerpts are the typographic ones used on the source pages. Both documents are organisational statements presumably under copyright; excerpts are all under 30 words. Grace axis: the tradition's representative statements combine total depravity and eternal security with Christ dying 'for all mankind' and salvation 'received by personal faith', and are silent on unconditional election, which is consistent with the audited 48; individual Bible churches range from four-point Calvinist to explicitly non-Calvinist, and no single document settles it. Worship axis: no statement on worship form was found in either document; the autonomy article is offered only as indirect support. The IFCA site also links a 'Historical Resolutions 1955-2024' PDF (https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6455103057a5064f6995a619/68ae13dcbede78afd290ff75_IFCA%20Historical%20Resolutions%201955-2024.pdf) which was not opened and might hold a resolution on worship or on the charismatic movement.
